extracted.intended_audience: Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences graduate students seeking fellowship funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for GSAS graduate students on finding and preparing applications for internal and external fellowships to support research, language study, graduate study, and dissertation writing. Covers where to search, typical required materials, timelining, and available advising resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship proposal (project statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship proposal, explaining your research topic and what you plan to do if you are granted the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate the significance of your fellowship project; draft your proposal early to get as much feedback as possible. The Fellowships & Writing Center provides feedback on articulating significance and will read and return essays after completing the FWC intake form, offering appointments to discuss feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation letters are commonly required for fellowship competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan your application well in advance by seeking out recommenders early to ensure they can write timely, thoughtful letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget of expected expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A budget of expenses you expect to incur, especially for fellowships requiring travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a clear, realistic budget aligned to the fellowship period and activities; include travel, research, and other project-specific costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts are typically requested as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain official transcripts well ahead of deadlines to avoid delays in submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum vitae (CV) content
rubrics_metrics.description: A current CV, which includes a list of awards and fellowships you have won during your time as a graduate student, presentations, publications, and other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep your CV up to date and tailored to highlight achievements and experiences relevant to the fellowship; document presentations, publications, and prior awards clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan Ahead: Deadlines for fellowship competitions are usually in the academic year before the fellowship period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For funding for the fall or spring, apply the previous fall. Plan applications well in advance to secure recommenders, transcripts, and to allow time for proposal drafting and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match eligibility and opportunity filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CARAT to search for fellowship opportunities by keyword, citizenship requirement, length of opportunity, stage in graduate school, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make CARAT your first stop to identify opportunities that match your eligibility and stage; verify citizenship or other eligibility requirements before investing time in an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of institutional and external databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Search internal and external databases for fellowship opportunities (e.g., CARAT, University of Illinois Fellowship Finder, UCLA Search for Graduate and Postdoc Funding, University of Chicago Fellowships Database, Online Guide to Scholarships & Resources for LGBTQIA+ College Students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden your search across multiple databases and specialized guides to uncover discipline-specific and demographic-targeted opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek advising and writing support
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Help: The Fellowships & Writing Center provides guidance, individual consultations, and essay critiques for fellowship proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the FWC intake form to get essay review and schedule appointments; sign up for advising appointments with named staff (e.g., Jeannette Miller) for questions about fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow specific fellowship instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Every fellowship has specific criteria and application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read and follow each competition's application instructions and evaluation criteria rather than relying solely on general guidance; tailor materials to what the specific fellowship requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of previous awards and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Document awards, fellowships, presentations, and publications in application materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list and contextualize prior honors and scholarly activity to demonstrate preparedness and track record relevant to the proposed project.
